prompt: A random sample of $36$ college students sleeps an average of $\bar{x} = 7.5$ hours per night with standard deviation $s = 1.2$ hours. Construct a $95\%$ confidence interval for the mean nightly sleep of all students at the college, using $t^* = 2.030$ (df $= 35$). What is the UPPER endpoint? Round to two decimal places.
hint: The interval is the sample mean plus or minus a margin of error, and the upper endpoint uses the plus sign.

hints.text: The interval is the sample mean plus or minus a margin of error, and the upper endpoint uses the plus sign.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Warm up: $\bar{x} = 10$, $s = 2$, $n = 4$, $t^* = 3$: SE $= 2/2 = 1$, ME $= 3$, upper endpoint $13$. Same three steps here.
The standard error is $1.2/\sqrt{36} = 0.2$ and the margin of error is $2.030 \times 0.2$. Add that margin to $7.5$.
The margin of error is $0.406$, so the upper endpoint is $7.5 + 0.406 = 7.906$, about $7.91$ hours.

explanation: The conditions hold: the sample is random, and $n = 36 \ge 30$ makes the $t$ procedure safe even without a normal population.
The standard error is $s/\sqrt{n} = 1.2/6 = 0.2$, and the margin of error is $2.030 \times 0.2 = 0.406$.
The interval is $7.5 \pm 0.406 = (7.094, 7.906)$, so the upper endpoint is about $7.91$ hours.

alternativeExplanations.title: Say what it means
steps: We are $95\%$ confident the true mean sleep for all students at this college is between $7.09$ and $7.91$ hours.
Notice the interval is about the MEAN, not about any individual student, many of whom sleep far outside this range.
The upper endpoint, $7.91$, is the most the average could plausibly be given this sample.
